title: Human receptors for sweet and umami taste
authors: Li X, Staszewski L, Xu H, Durick K, Zoller M, Adler E
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
population: HEK-293-derived cells expressing human or rat T1R2 and T1R3 with G alpha 15 or a G alpha 15/i1 chimera
authorConflicts: The authors are affiliated with Senomyx, Inc. and Aurora Biosciences Corporation, La Jolla and San Diego.
result: Cells co-expressing human T1R2 and T1R3 responded to sucrose, which cells expressing either subunit alone did not, and to every other sweet stimulus tested: fructose, galactose, glucose, lactose and maltose, glycine and D-tryptophan, monellin and thaumatin, and acesulfame K, aspartame, cyclamate, dulcin, neotame, saccharin and sucralose; lactisole inhibited the response. Rat T1R2/T1R3 did not respond to aspartame or monellin, which rodents do not find palatable.
